name: Thistledown Vale
summary: A green, rain-soft valley where magic is the quiet work of daily life — hearth-charms, hedge-witchery, and ward-signs scratched over every door. Low chimneys, water-wheels, and lantern-light; no powder, little steel. The vale is ringed by the old Warden Stones that keep the Whistling Woods and its Hollow Folk at a polite distance. Lately, one of the Wardens has cracked.

lore.title: The Green Weave
lore.body: Magic in the vale is small and woven into craft: coaxing dough to rise, mending a snapped axle, keeping a flame from guttering, scratching a ward-sign over a cradle. The folk call it the Green Weave, and it answers best to patience, season, and a fair bargain. True sorcery — fire from empty hands — is a thing of stories and the deep woods.

lore.title: The Warden Stones
lore.body: Seven standing stones ring Thistledown Vale, set so long ago no one recalls the hands that raised them. They are the vale's fence against the Hollow Folk and the colder things that sleep in the barrows. The Hedge-Circle tends them, renewing the ward-signs each turning of the year. A cracked Warden is an open gate.

lore.title: The Whistling Woods
lore.body: East past the Old Ford the trees crowd close and the wind threads the branches into something like voices. The Hollow Folk dwell there — not cruel, exactly, but bound by old manners and older bargains, and quick to collect on a careless promise. Iron bites them; honesty confuses them; a gift freely given buys safe passage.

lore.title: Brackenford
lore.body: The vale's heart: a market village at the ford over the Bracken brook, all thatch and woodsmoke around a muddy green. The Gilded Hart pours the only ale worth the walk, Emrin's hammer keeps a steady beat, and the Bracken Mill grinds the vale's bread — or it did, until the miller failed to come home.

factions.name: The Hedge-Circle
factions.description: The loose sisterhood of witches, ward-wrights, and hedge-keepers who tend the vale's small magics and the Warden Stones. They teach by apprenticeship and answer to no lord.
goals: Pass the craft to willing hands
Keep a fair bargain with the woods

factions.name: The Reeve's Hall
factions.description: Brackenford's plain-spoken governance — the Reeve and the village moot. Slow to act, fond of waiting for spring, but loyal to the folk.

factions.name: The Hollow Folk
factions.description: The fae of the Whistling Woods. Neither friends nor foes — keepers of old pacts, collectors of curiosities and careless words. They want their woods left to themselves and their bargains honored.

locations.name: The Gilded Hart
locations.description: Low beams, a banked fire, and the smell of barley and woodsmoke. A carved stag's head hangs over the hearth, gilt worn to brass. The warmest room in Brackenford after dark.

locations.name: Brackenford Green
locations.description: A muddy commons ringed by thatched stalls, a stone well, and a leaning maypole. Footpaths run to the inn, the forge, the mill-road, and down to the ford. Ward-signs are chalked above every door.

locations.name: Emrin's Forge
locations.description: Heat and the ring of iron. Horseshoes, hinges, and ward-nails hang in rows. Emrin keeps a bowl of cold iron filings by the door — a hedge against the Hollow Folk, he'll say, if you ask.

locations.name: The Bracken Mill
locations.description: A timber mill astride the brook, its great wheel still and dripping. Sacks of flour slump in the dark, and the air smells faintly wrong — sour, like milk left in the sun.

locations.name: The Old Ford
locations.description: Flat stones cross the Bracken where the brook runs shallow. On the far bank the trees begin. The wind off the water carries a thin, threadlike whistling from the woods beyond.

locations.name: Eaves of the Whistling Woods
locations.description: The trees lean inward and the light goes green and dim. Paths appear that weren't there a moment ago. Somewhere ahead, the standing stones of the Warden Barrow show grey through the trunks.

exits.name: a game trail into the deep wood

locations.name: The Warden Barrow
locations.description: A ring of seven moss-furred stones around a low grass mound. One stone is split top to base, the ward-signs broken across the crack, and from the dark seam breathes a cold that the summer can't touch.

npcs.name: Maelle Ashfield
npcs.summary: A hedge-witch of the Circle, grey-eyed and unhurried, who has felt the Wardens weaken before and means to mend this one before the moot finishes arguing.
npcs.persona: Warm but blunt, patient with people and impatient with delay. She explains the craft plainly, names a danger without dressing it up, and tends to lead simply by standing and walking toward the trouble. She'd rather be wrong and moving than right and waiting.
npcs.appearance: A travel-worn green shawl pinned with a hawthorn brooch, charm-cords at both wrists, mud to the knee.
goals: Keep the folk of Brackenford safe
knowledge: The Warden Stones and their ward-signs
The manners and bargains of the Hollow Folk
Every footpath and hedge in the vale

npcs.name: Dorran Webb
npcs.summary: A young hunter who trails Maelle like a faithful hound, quick with a bow and quicker to fill a silence.
npcs.persona: Eager, loyal, and a little too talkative. He knows the woods' game-trails better than anyone his age and is desperate to prove it. He looks to Maelle for cues and to the player for approval.
npcs.appearance: A patched oilskin, a yew bow worn smooth, a fox-tail charm at his belt.
goals: See the woods and come back to tell of it
knowledge: The game-trails and where the deer water
Which berries kill and which only sting

npcs.name: Bett Hollow
npcs.summary: The Gilded Hart's innkeeper, who hears everything over her taps and forgets none of it.
npcs.persona: Motherly, shrewd, and incurably fond of gossip. She fusses over travelers, waters no ale, and trades news for news.
npcs.appearance: Flour-dusted apron, grey braid, a wooden spoon she gestures with like a wand.
goals: Keep her inn warm and full
knowledge: Who came and went and when
The night the miller didn't come home
Where the best woods-honey is gathered

npcs.name: Emrin Stout
npcs.summary: The village smith, terse and iron-fair, who trusts cold iron more than charms.
npcs.persona: Few words, none of them wasted. He keeps iron filings at his door and a low opinion of the woods. Fair in a bargain, immovable when he's decided.
npcs.appearance: Burn-scarred forearms, a leather apron, a perpetual squint.
goals: Keep iron between Brackenford and the woods
knowledge: Who in the village owes whom
How to hurt a Hollow thing

npcs.name: Wren
npcs.summary: The miller's daughter, holding the silent mill together since her father walked out toward the ford and never came back.
npcs.persona: Sharp-tongued out of fear, exhausted, and trying not to hope. She'll snap at pity and soften at help.
npcs.appearance: Flour in her dark hair, her father's too-big coat, raw hands.
goals: Keep the mill from being given to someone else
Not break in front of anyone
knowledge: The wrong smell in the new flour

npcs.name: Thistle
npcs.summary: A hollow-lad of the Whistling Woods who lingers at the eaves, trading riddles and curiosities, bound by manners older than the village.
npcs.persona: Speaks in sideways riddles and fair-sounding bargains, neither friend nor foe. Delighted by curiosities, confused by plain honesty, and scrupulous about a promise once made. Will not lie, but will not volunteer.
npcs.appearance: Too tall, too thin, bark-brown skin and eyes like still pond-water; a coat sewn from leaves that are always the wrong season.
goals: See what the cracked stone lets out
knowledge: What walks the woods after dark
What the Wardens were truly built to hold

monsters.name: Mist Cat
monsters.description: A long, soft-footed hunter the grey of river fog, near invisible until it moves. It stalks the ford at dusk and fears fire and iron.

monsters.name: Boggart
monsters.description: A house-fae gone sour, turned from helpful to spiteful. It curdles milk, snarls thread, and bites in the dark. A gift or a kind word can still turn it.

monsters.name: Barrow Wight
monsters.description: A cold, slow-stirring thing the Wardens were raised to hold, roused now by the broken stone. It hates warmth and living breath, and the chill of it stops the heart before its hands ever land.

items.name: Warded Lantern
items.description: A tin lantern scratched with the Circle's signs. Its flame never gutters, even in the wind off the woods.

items.name: Hedge-Charm Cord
items.description: A braided cord of red wool, hawthorn, and a single iron bead — a minor ward the Hedge-Circle gives to friends.

items.name: Iron Knife
items.description: A plain knife of cold-worked iron, dull but honest. Iron bites the Hollow Folk where steel and spell slide off.

items.name: Hunting Bow
items.description: A well-kept yew bow, the grip worn pale. Dorran's spare, lent to a steady hand.

items.name: Honeyed Cakes
items.description: Bett's small dense cakes, sticky with woods-honey. A bite is worth a warm hearth and a held breath.

items.name: Chipped Warden-Stone
items.description: A fist of grey stone broken from the cracked Warden, the carved ward-sign split clean through. It hums faintly, and the air around it is cold.

items.name: Sealed Missive
items.description: A folded square of good paper, still sealed with a blot of grey wax pressed with a tinker's-cog sigil. It was in your pack when you woke — you do not remember it being handed to you.

properties.body: To the tinker wintering in the vale — you do not know me, but I know your hands. A thing of mine broke in a way no hedge-charm will mend, and I dare not carry it to the moot. Come to the old kiln above Brackenford before the next dark of the moon, and come alone. Bring your tools. — a friend you have not met

items.name: Road-Courier's Letter
items.description: A travel-stained letter a road-courier pressed into your hand, sealed with a smear of green wax and addressed in a hurried hand to 'whoever the vale can spare.'

properties.body: To whoever the vale can spare — Gorse Hill sends word and little hope. Our well has soured the way yours has, and two of ours walked the miller's road into the Whistling Woods and did not come back. We have no hedge-witch left who dares the crossing. If any soul in Brackenford will come and see what has taken root between our valleys, come by the ford-road, and come soon. — Elder Sawney of Gorse Hill

spells.name: Mending Charm
spells.description: Coax a broken small thing — a cord, a cup, a snapped haft — back toward whole.

spells.name: Hearthlight
spells.description: Call a warm, steady light to hand or hearth that no wind can snuff.

spells.name: Green-Coaxing
spells.description: Persuade growing things to hurry — to bind a path shut, part a thicket, or ripen a fruit out of season.

spells.name: Ward-Sign
spells.description: Scratch or trace a protective sign that turns aside the uncanny for a time.

spells.name: Mist-Veil
spells.description: Draw a concealing mist about yourself and those near, softening shape and sound.

gazetteer.name: Gorse Hill
gazetteer.summary: the next vale's market town, a day west along the drove road, where Brackenford's wool goes to be weighed

gazetteer.name: The Seventh Warden
gazetteer.summary: the far Warden Stone up on the northern fells — the one the Hedge-Circle stopped tending, and stopped explaining why

gazetteer.name: Rushdown Fen
gazetteer.summary: the drowned meadows downstream where the Bracken loses its way — boggart country, rich in eels and bad bargains

gazetteer.name: The Hollow Market
gazetteer.summary: the Hollow Folk's moonlit fair, deep past the eaves of the Whistling Woods — reached by invitation, or by a careless promise
